idiom_name: function types for plain commands; interface with execute()/undo() for history; discriminated union with exhaustive switch for data commands
implementation_notes: TypeScript builds on JavaScript's functions as command values - a function type expression or a call signature fully describes the contract - and adds compile-time structure exactly where the classic pattern earns it: an interface with execute() and an optional undo() for a typed history, or a discriminated union of request records plus a switch that narrowing keeps exhaustive. Prefer the union form when commands must be serialised, logged or validated at a boundary and the interface form when commands carry behaviour and an inverse.
pitfalls: An interface cannot prevent a command from mutating shared state; mark captured fields readonly and keep commands immutable so history entries stay replayable.
Exhaustiveness only holds while the switch narrows on the discriminant and ends in a never assignment - a default branch silently absorbs newly added variants.
Optional undo() makes the inverse easy to forget: either require it for history-bound commands or model reversible and irreversible commands as separate types.
Functions are erased after a JSON round-trip, so anything persisted or replayed must be the data form, never a closure.
